name: BOMB CALORIMETER
desc: Microprocessor-Based Fully Automatic Bomb Calorimeter utilizing the highly accurate Isoperibol measurement method to evaluate the calorific value of solid and liquid fuels. Features an ultra-high temperature resolution of 0.01°C, a big jumbo 20x4 blue LCD display, and a built-in thermal printer.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS BOMB CALORIMETER is a microprocessor-based, fully automatic isoperibol calorimeter engineered for the precise determination of gross calorific value (GCV) in solid and liquid fuels. It employs the isoperibol measurement principle, where the calorimeter vessel is maintained at a constant jacket temperature while the temperature rise of the water bath is tracked with a high-precision electronic Beckmann thermometer array, achieving a resolution of 0.01°C. This instrument is indispensable for fuel testing laboratories, power plants, coal mines, and research institutions. B.Sc and M.Sc students use it to understand thermochemistry and energy content of materials; PhD researchers and chemists rely on it for characterizing novel fuels, biomass, and waste-derived energy sources. The bomb is charged with high-purity oxygen (typically 30 bar) to ensure complete combustion of samples such as coal, coke, fuel oil, diesel, biomass pellets, and even food products for caloric content. Calibration is performed using certified benzoic acid (e.g., NIST SRM 39j) to determine the effective heat capacity of the system. The instrument complies with international standards including ASTM D240, ASTM D5865, ISO 1928, and DIN 51900, ensuring traceable and reproducible results. Its automated gas filling system, built-in thermal printer, and data logging software make it a robust tool for both routine quality control and advanced research in energy science.
sop: Ensure the instrument is placed on a stable, level bench and connected to a 220 V AC, 50 Hz power supply with proper earthing.
Prepare the sample: weigh approximately 0.5–1.0 g of the solid or liquid fuel into a clean combustion crucible using an analytical balance, and record the exact mass.

Attach a known length of fuse wire (e.g., 10 cm cotton thread or nickel-chromium wire) to the electrodes inside the bomb head, ensuring it makes contact with the sample without touching the crucible walls.
Assemble the bomb by carefully lowering the head into the bomb cylinder, then tighten the sealing ring securely using the provided spanner.
Fill the bomb with high-purity oxygen using the automated Push-n-Fit gas filling system to a pressure of 30 bar (or as specified in the method), ensuring no leaks.
Place the charged bomb into the calorimeter vessel, which contains a precisely measured volume of distilled water (typically 2000 mL) at a known temperature.
Close the calorimeter lid and connect the ignition leads and temperature sensor.
On the control panel, press the 'SET' button once to enter the parameter setting mode.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter, such as the sample mass, water equivalent, or calibration factor, as prompted on the LCD.
Press 'SET' again to lock the value and proceed to the next parameter or exit the setting mode.
Initiate the measurement by pressing the 'START' button; the instrument will automatically monitor the temperature, fire the bomb, and track the temperature rise until equilibrium is reached.

After the measurement is complete, the LCD will display the calculated calorific value; press the 'PRINT' button to generate a hard copy report with date and time stamp from the built-in thermal printer.
Open the calorimeter, carefully remove the bomb, release the residual gas pressure using the vent valve, and disassemble the bomb to inspect for complete combustion (no soot or unburned residue).
Clean the bomb, crucible, and electrodes with distilled water and dry thoroughly before the next test.

SAFETY WARNING: Always wear safety goggles, heat-resistant gloves, and a lab coat when handling the bomb and oxygen cylinder. Never exceed the recommended oxygen pressure (typically 30 bar) and never open the bomb immediately after firing; wait for the pressure to be released and the bomb to cool to room temperature to avoid explosive decompression or burns.
